dor_checklist_results.item: Verified real file paths from codebase grounding
Concrete integration spec with existing API contracts

assumptions_made.assumption: The session token is stored as a cookie, not in localStorage, based on reading apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts line 34.
assumptions_made.rationale: Cookie-based storage is the existing pattern in the middleware. Implementing session refresh via cookie avoids any localStorage security concerns and is consistent with the current architecture.

assumptions_made.assumption: The dashboard at apps/web/src/pages/dashboard.tsx is the primary authenticated surface requiring the session-refresh flow.
assumptions_made.rationale: Reading apps/web/src/pages/ reveals dashboard.tsx is the only page with a session-dependent data fetch on mount. Other pages are either public or delegate to dashboard layout.

alternatives_considered.option: Short-lived tokens with silent refresh via a background /refresh endpoint
alternatives_considered.analysis: Keeps the session alive without user interruption. Requires implementing a background interval in the client. Most secure option — tokens expire quickly even if leaked. Recommended for V1 because the infrastructure already has a /refresh stub in sessions.ts.
Simpler implementation but increases breach window if a token is stolen. Not recommended because it conflicts with the product vision's security posture for an enterprise-facing tool.

ui_ux_notes: The user should experience no interruption when the session is refreshed silently. On explicit logout, the session cookie must be cleared and the user redirected to /login. Error state (refresh failed) should show a non-blocking banner prompting re-login, not a hard redirect that loses form state.
recommended_next_step: Issue is ready for implementation. Implementer should claim via status:ready -> status:in-progress and follow the behavior contract in the issue body.
